title: Fusilli alla Caprese
subtitle: Fusilli tossed with a quick fresh tomato and mozzarella sauce
excerpt: Fusilli alla caprese is the hot version of the classic Caprese combination: fusilli tossed with a quick sauce of fresh tomatoes, garlic, olive oil, and torn mozzarella added at the last moment so it melts slightly into the pasta. It is a summer dish that takes 20 minutes and needs good tomatoes.
sourceNotes: The Caprese combination of tomato, mozzarella, and basil originates from the island of Capri in Campania. Applied to hot pasta, it is a home-cooking staple across southern Italy in summer, when fresh tomatoes and mozzarella are at their best.

content.text: Fusilli alla caprese is a hot summer pasta: a quick tomato sauce with garlic and olive oil, tossed with fusilli and finished with torn mozzarella that melts into the warm pasta just enough to become creamy without disappearing. The mozzarella must go in off the heat: it needs to melt slightly, not cook through to rubber. Use ripe, sweet summer tomatoes.

Warm the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the garlic for 2 minutes until pale gold. Add the tomatoes and season well. Cook for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring occasionally and breaking up the tomatoes, until the sauce has reduced and concentrated.
Stir in most of the basil. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Cook the fusilli in well-salted boiling water until 1 minute short of al dente. Reserve a cup of pasta water, then drain.

Toss the fusilli into the sauce with a splash of pasta water over high heat for 1 minute. Remove from heat. Add the torn mozzarella and remaining basil, tossing gently. The mozzarella will melt slightly. Serve immediately.

items.cause: Added while the pan was still on the heat
items.fix: Take the pan completely off the heat before adding mozzarella. It should soften and melt slightly from residual warmth, not cook.

items.cause: Out-of-season tomatoes with high water content, or not reduced long enough
items.fix: Reduce the sauce further. If using tomatoes with high water content, drain some of the juice from the chopped tomatoes before cooking.

items.cause: Sauce is too thin to cling to the spiral shape
items.fix: Reduce the sauce until it is thick enough to coat the pasta. The spiral shape needs a slightly thicker sauce to cling in its ridges.

content.text: The caprese combination of tomato, mozzarella, basil, and olive oil comes from the island of Capri. It reflects the Campanian tradition of using a few good ingredients together. Applied to hot pasta it becomes alla caprese. This is a standard summer dish in Campanian home kitchens. The mozzarella melts slightly into the hot pasta, which sets it apart from a cold dressed version.
